about: The host's frame diagnostics (frame-diagnostics.h; sample/FrameProbe.tsx; docs/performance.mdx, "Reading the session's log"): a frame whose work takes longer than a refresh of its display writes one line to the session's log naming what started it and where its time went (JavaScript holding the thread 120 ms after a press: its JavaScript at least 100 ms, its refreshes dropped), at most one a second with how many went unsaid; presses answered at once write none, and 90 frames of requestAnimationFrame stay within a refresh (every run checks a frame is said to be slow exactly when its work passes a refresh); and while the window draws, a summary every 10 s whose numbers are those of the frames in its report (regress.py checks every summary of every run), and none while it is idle.

steps.name: a press answered at once: no slow frame
a press whose JavaScript holds the thread 120 ms: one slow line, its time in JavaScript, its refreshes dropped
three such presses within a second: three slow frames, one line
the next slow line says the two not shown
90 frames of requestAnimationFrame, each drawn: nearly all within a refresh
idle: the frames since the last summary summed up once, within 10 s of the first, then nothing

logged: ^\[host so\.oxy\.frameprobe\] in the last 1\d\.\d s: \d+ frames, their work [\d.]+ ms median
